sections.subtitle: Match context
sections.text: Selhurst Park hosts a mid-table meeting: Crystal Palace sit 14th (39 points) and Newcastle United 13th (42 points). Sofascore model: home win 34%, draw 30%, away win 36%, both teams to score 43%. The market view is evenly split with a slight away lean and a lower chance of both sides scoring.

sections.subtitle: Current form
sections.text: Palace are unbeaten in 5 and have tightened up at the back, including 3 clean sheets in their last 4; they generated strong expected goals against AEK Larnaca (3.61) and Fiorentina (3.05). Newcastle’s last 5 read 1-1-3, conceding 13, though they did win 1-0 at Chelsea. Ismaïla Sarr is in form for Palace (5 goals in his last 5).

sections.subtitle: Head-to-head
sections.text: Newcastle have won the last 2 meetings at St James’ Park (2-0, 5-0), leading the recent series (last 5: Newcastle 3 wins, Palace 1, 1 draw). Malick Thiaw starred in January’s 2-0 (Sofascore 9.6). Kieran Trippier has been influential across recent clashes (average 8.02 rating, 2 assists).

sections.subtitle: Season stats snapshot
sections.text: Palace defend well (35 conceded, 11 clean sheets; both 3rd-best) but finish poorly against expectation (xG 45.8 vs 33 goals; large underperformance). They create a fair volume of big chances (76, 7th) but convert only 36% (15th) and have 49 big chances missed. Headers are a weapon (9 scored, 5th).

sections.subtitle: Tactical notes and key players
sections.text: Palace’s supply line runs through Adam Wharton (11 big chances created, league rank 4) and wide runners to target Newcastle’s full-back zones. Newcastle rely on Anthony Gordon’s direct threat and Trippier’s delivery, while Thiaw adds set-piece presence. Newcastle list Bruno Guimarães and Fabian Schär as missing, which may affect ball progression and aerial security.

sections.subtitle: Referee, cards and corners
sections.text: Referee Andy Madley averages 3.1 yellows and 0.11 reds per match. Head-to-head trends show more than 4.5 cards in 5 of the last 6, but Palace have seen fewer than 10.5 corners in 8 of 9 at home. Expect moderate discipline (around 3–5 yellows) and corners likely in single digits to low double figures.

sections.subtitle: Match prediction
sections.text: With Palace’s defence strong and finishing variance still an issue, and Newcastle carrying a slight model edge, a low-scoring contest suits the visitors marginally. Newcastle to edge it narrowly, with at least one side likely to keep a clean sheet.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Match context
halftimeSections.text: Newcastle United lead 1-0 at Selhurst Park after William Osula’s left‑foot finish on 43 minutes. The away side controlled possession (61-39) and generated the clearer chance profile, but Crystal Palace produced more shots on target (3-2) and finished the half strongly before being punished close to the interval.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Key half-time stats
halftimeSections.text: Expected goals: Newcastle 0.98, Crystal Palace 0.42. Shots on target: 2-3. Big chances: 1-1 (Palace missed theirs; Newcastle converted). Final-third entries: Palace 41, Newcastle 31. Penalty-area entries: 13-14. Possessions won in the final third: 5-1. Aerial and ground duels were near even (50-50 and 49-51 splits), reflecting a balanced physical contest.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Attack momentum
halftimeSections.text: Crystal Palace opened with intent and then weathered a long mid-half period of Newcastle control. From around 36 minutes Palace sustained their best attacking spell, creating pressure and territory, before Newcastle swung momentum back just before the break and scored during their strongest phase.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Tactical outlook
halftimeSections.text: Crystal Palace are getting joy down the right with Daniel Muñoz (2 shots on target) and Yéremy Pino (1 key pass, 1 big chance created). Faster deliveries into Jørgen Strand Larsen and second balls around the box should raise chance quality, as Palace already lead in final-third presence and high regains. Newcastle will be comfortable managing territory and breaking through wide runners Anthony Gordon and Jacob Murphy, with Osula’s movement targeting centre-backs on quick transitions. Set plays remain a route for both, with even aerial duels and clearances from Malick Thiaw and Sven Botman indicating a compact Newcastle block that Palace must disrupt with earlier crosses and cut-backs.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Players and match-ups
halftimeSections.text: For Palace, Muñoz’s underlaps and Pino’s supply look the clearest route to an equaliser. Jaydee Canvot’s missed big chance underlines space at the back post if Palace switch play quicker. For Newcastle, Gordon attacking the inside channel off Lewis Hall’s overlaps can isolate Palace’s full-back, while Osula remains the primary threat between the posts after a high-quality first-half chance.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Referee, cards and corners
halftimeSections.text: Corners are level (1-1). No cards are recorded in the first-half data. With Palace set to push and Newcastle likely to counter, expect corners to rise and a higher chance of cautions if the duels continue at current intensity.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Second-half path
halftimeSections.text: Palace have the pressing platform to force errors and raise shot volume, while Newcastle have the lead and the more efficient chance creation so far. If Palace maintain the right-sided combinations and improve the timing of entries into the box, an equaliser is plausible. Newcastle’s best route to a second goal remains fast breaks into wide spaces rather than sustained possession.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Match prediction
halftimeSections.text: Crystal Palace to find a second-half equaliser, with Newcastle holding firm thereafter. Predicted final score: 1-1. Next goal: Crystal Palace.
